interest: Shows 1938 Japanese discount war-risk insurance to win rubber/tin shipping, amid Munich-crisis market panic in Singapore.
overview: September 1938 Singapore telegram: Japan offered 50%-discount war-risk insurance on rubber and tin shipped via Pacific or Panama routes on Japanese ships, with no takers, amid falling rubber prices and securities selloff on fears war would end rubber restrictions; Feis relayed this to Rubber Manufacturers Association president Viles for comment.

subfiles.about: Reporting Japanese offers of discounted war risk insurance on shipments carried by Japanese vessels and a fall in Singapore rubber prices caused by European war expectations.
subfiles.summary: Singapore telegram: Japanese underwriters offered war-risk insurance on rubber and tin cargoes at half rates for shipment on Japanese vessels, with no acceptances; rubber prices fell to 21 Straits cents amid fears restriction quotas would collapse in war, dragging down local securities.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Singapore on Japanese War Risk Insurance and Rubber Market Collapse

subfiles.about: Transmitting Singapore intelligence regarding Japanese discounted war risk insurance and rubber market declines to the Rubber Manufacturers Association and requesting industry feedback.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis (Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Feis forwards Singapore's reports to Viles of the Rubber Manufacturers Association: Japanese firms offered 50%-discount war-risk insurance on rubber and tin via Pacific/Panama routes on Japanese ships, with no takers, amid falling rubber prices and securities, fearing rubber restrictions would end in a European war; Feis asks for his views.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to A. L. Viles on Japanese War Risk Insurance and Rubber Restrictions
subfiles.to: A. L. Viles (President, Rubber Manufacturers Association)
